subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec/sandbox access boundary, or remain a visibility-only skill eligibility setting?
rationale: The issue asks to change a public security expectation for skill configuration and tool execution, which affects operator trust, upgrade behavior, and multiple runtime enforcement surfaces.

options.title: Make disabled skills a hard boundary
options.body: Treat disabled skill directories as denied for relevant read and execution paths, with tests and docs making the stricter security semantics explicit.

options.title: Add a separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled: false` visibility-only for compatibility and introduce an explicit security knob for deployments that need disabled-skill filesystem and exec isolation.

options.title: Document visibility-only semantics
options.body: Close the security expectation gap by explicitly stating that skill disabling hides skills from discovery but does not restrict host filesystem or shell access.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat disabled skill directories as denied for relevant read and execution paths, with tests and docs making the stricter security semantics explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily a security and exec-boundary policy choice, and this owner appears in recent adjacent security and exec history.
